title: Reduction is bijective on morphisms of finite etale algebras
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and S,T finite etale R-algebras [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Reduction gives a bijection from R-algebra homomorphisms S to T to kappa-algebra homomorphisms $\kappa\otimes_R S$ to $\kappa\otimes_R T$.

proof.text: (The functor.) Write $\mathcal C$ for the category of finite etale $R$-algebras and $\mathcal D$ for that of finite etale $\kappa$-algebras, $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $F(S)=S/\mathfrak mS$, $F(\varphi)=\overline\varphi=\varphi\bmod\mathfrak m$. $F$ is well defined: $S/\mathfrak mS$ is generated as a $\kappa$-vector space by the images of $R$-module generators of $S$, so it is finite over $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(S/\mathfrak mS)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak m)$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quotient-base-change] (with $I=\mathfrak m$). $F$ preserves finite products: $(S_1\times\cdots\times S_r)/\mathfrak m(S_1\times\cdots\times S_r)=\prod_jS_j/\mathfrak mS_j$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, lines 42457-42505), the functor of the statement (line 42458)

proof.text: (Objects of $\mathcal C$ split into local pieces with field reductions.) Let $S$ be a finite etale $R$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] (Stacks 04GG (1)$\Rightarrow$(8)) $R$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-retraction-finite-product-local] (04GG (8)$\Rightarrow$(10)), so $S\cong A_1\times\cdots\times A_n$ ($n\ge0$) with $A_i$ local; this is the decomposition the source takes from 04GG (10) (or 04GJ). Each $A_i\cong S_{e_i}$ for the idempotent $e_i$ of the $i$-th factor, so $A_i$ is a finitely generated $R$-module (a quotient of $S$) and $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] (2). Let $\mathfrak n_i$ be the maximal ideal of $A_i$. Since $A_i$ is finite over the local ring $R$, $\mathfrak n_i\cap R=\mathfrak m$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]. By Stacks 00U4 (1) [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal], $\mathfrak m(A_i)_{\mathfrak n_i}=\mathfrak n_i(A_i)_{\mathfrak n_i}$; as $A_i$ is local, $(A_i)_{\mathfrak n_i}=A_i$, so $\mathfrak mA_i=\mathfrak n_i$ and $A_i/\mathfrak mA_i=\kappa(\mathfrak n_i)$ is a field, finite separable over $\kappa$ by 00U4 (2) [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable]. Hence $F(S)\cong\prod_iA_i/\mathfrak mA_i$ is the decomposition of $F(S)$ into fields, and the only prime of $A_i$ containing $\mathfrak mA_i$ is $\mathfrak n_i$. (The source says '$A_i$ local and finite etale over $S$'; it means over $R$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, lines 42457-42505), lines 42460-42469 (Lemma 04GG part (10), Lemma 00U4)

proof.text: (Objects of $\mathcal D$; the canonical decomposition.) A finite etale $\kappa$-algebra is isomorphic to a finite product of fields, each a finite separable extension of $\kappa$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. A local ring and a field have no idempotents other than $0,1$. For a ring $T\neq0$ whose only idempotents are $0,1$ and a finite product $P=P_1\times\cdots\times P_n$, every ring map $P\to T$ factors through exactly one projection $P\to P_i$: the images of the standard idempotents $\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n$ are orthogonal idempotents of $T$ with sum $1$, so exactly one of them is $1$ and the others are $0$. Consequently the factors of such a decomposition are indexed by the primitive idempotents, with unique factor isomorphisms compatible with the projections (abstract factors may have nontrivial automorphisms), and $\operatorname{Hom}(\prod_iP_i,\prod_jT_j)=\prod_j\coprod_i\operatorname{Hom}(P_i,T_j)$ for rings $T_j\ne0$ without nontrivial idempotents, both for $R$-algebras and for $\kappa$-algebras. By step 2 these decompositions of $S$ and of $F(S)$ correspond under $F$, and by step 1 $F$ is compatible with the identification of Hom sets. So $F$ is fully faithful as soon as $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S_1,S_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_\kappa(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$, $\varphi\mapsto\overline\varphi$, is bijective for finite etale $S_1,S_2$ with $\kappa_i=S_i/\mathfrak mS_i$ fields (equivalently, by step 2, $S_1,S_2$ local).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, lines 42457-42505), lines 42470-42472 ('every object of C and D decomposes canonically into irreducible pieces which correspond via the given functor'); the reduction is written out here

proof.text: (The tensor product.) Let $S_1,S_2$ be finite etale over $R$ with $\kappa_1,\kappa_2$ fields. $T=S_1\otimes_RS_2$ is a finitely generated $R$-module (generated by the $x\otimes y$ for generators $x$, $y$ of $S_1$, $S_2$); $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}S_2$ is etale by base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], hence $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale as a composite [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). By step 2, $T=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n$ with $A_i$ local finite etale over $R$ and $\overline A_i=A_i/\mathfrak mA_i$ fields, and $T/\mathfrak mT=(S_1\otimes_RS_2)\otimes_R\kappa\cong\kappa_1\otimes_\kappa\kappa_2\cong\prod_i\overline A_i$. Write $p_i:T\to A_i$ for the projections and $j_i:S_2\to A_i$, $s\mapsto p_i(1\otimes s)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, lines 42457-42505), lines 42473-42480

proof.text: ($\operatorname{Hom}_R(S_1,S_2)$ is the set $I=\{i: j_i\text{ is an isomorphism}\}$.) For an $R$-algebra map $\varphi:S_1\to S_2$ let $\mu_\varphi:T\to S_2$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\varphi(x)y$ ('$\varphi\times1$'); it is surjective ($\mu_\varphi(1\otimes y)=y$), and $S_2$ is local, so by step 3 $\mu_\varphi=\pi\circ p_i$ for exactly one $i=i(\varphi)$ and a surjection $\pi:A_i\to S_2$ with $\pi\circ j_i=\mathrm{id}_{S_2}$. Then $A_i=j_i(S_2)\oplus K$ as $S_2$-modules, $K=\ker\pi$, and $K$ is a finitely generated $R$-module (a direct summand of $A_i$). Reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$, $\overline A_i=\kappa_2\oplus K/\mathfrak mK$ and $\overline\pi:\overline A_i\to\kappa_2$ is a surjective ring map of fields, hence injective, so $K/\mathfrak mK=0$, i.e. $K=\mathfrak mK$, and $K=0$ by Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] ($\mathfrak m$ is the Jacobson radical of $R$). So $\pi$ is an isomorphism, $j_i=\pi^{-1}$ and $i(\varphi)\in I$. Conversely for $i\in I$ put $\varphi_i=j_i^{-1}\circ p_i\circ(x\mapsto x\otimes1)$. Then $\varphi=\varphi_{i(\varphi)}$ (since $\mu_\varphi=j_{i}^{-1}\circ p_i$ and $\varphi(x)=\mu_\varphi(x\otimes1)$), and $i(\varphi_i)=i$ (the $R$-algebra maps $\mu_{\varphi_i}$ and $j_i^{-1}\circ p_i$ agree on all $x\otimes1$ and $1\otimes y$, hence are equal, and the latter factors through $p_i$). So $\varphi\mapsto i(\varphi)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S_1,S_2)\to I$.

proof.text: (The same over $\kappa$.) In exactly the same way, with $T/\mathfrak mT=\kappa_1\otimes_\kappa\kappa_2=\prod_i\overline A_i$, projections $\overline p_i$ and $\overline j_i:\kappa_2\to\overline A_i$, a $\kappa$-algebra map $\psi:\kappa_1\to\kappa_2$ gives the surjection $\mu_\psi:T/\mathfrak mT\to\kappa_2$, which factors through exactly one $\overline p_i$ (step 3) by a surjection of fields $\overline A_i\to\kappa_2$, automatically an isomorphism inverse to $\overline j_i$; and $\psi\mapsto i(\psi)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_\kappa(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)\to I'=\{i:\overline j_i\text{ is an isomorphism}\}$, with inverse $i\mapsto\overline j_i^{-1}\circ\overline p_i\circ(x\mapsto x\otimes1)$. Moreover $\mu_{\overline\varphi}=\mu_\varphi\bmod\mathfrak m$, so $i(\overline\varphi)=i(\varphi)$ for every $\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_R(S_1,S_2)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, lines 42457-42505), lines 42486-42489 ('in exactly the same way')

proof.text: ($I=I'$, hence full faithfulness.) If $j_i$ is an isomorphism so is $\overline j_i=j_i\bmod\mathfrak m$. Conversely let $\overline j_i$ be an isomorphism. $A_i$ is a finitely generated $R$-module and $A_i=j_i(S_2)+\mathfrak mA_i$, so $j_i$ is surjective by Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] (applied to $A_i/j_i(S_2)$). $A_i$ is flat over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and finitely generated, hence free [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free], so $j_i$ splits $R$-linearly: $S_2\cong A_i\oplus K'$ with $K'=\ker j_i$ finitely generated; modulo $\mathfrak m$, $\kappa_2\cong\overline A_i\oplus K'/\mathfrak mK'$ with $\overline j_i$ bijective, so $K'/\mathfrak mK'=0$ and $K'=0$ by Nakayama. So $I=I'$, and by steps 5 and 6 the map $\varphi\mapsto\overline\varphi$ is the composite of bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S_1,S_2)\to I=I'\to\operatorname{Hom}_\kappa(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$. With step 3, $F$ is fully faithful.
